key_insight: A deep neural network predicts noise figure in dual-pump fiber-optic phase-sensitive amplifiers about 400× faster than semi-quantum evaluation, with a reported MAE of 0.0015 dB.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate enables rapid amplifier design-space searches targeting 20 dB gain and 0.3 dB noise figure.
method: Generate simulated input–output data using a semi-quantum noise-figure framework.
Train an optimized deep neural network for rapid noise-figure prediction.
Use clustering to identify design parameters associated with target gain and noise figure.
evidence_signal: Evaluation against the semi-quantum approach reports approximately 400× lower computation time and 0.0015 dB mean absolute error on simulated data.
watch_item: Accuracy outside the simulated parameter space and agreement with physical experiments are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Deep-learning surrogate model for rapid quantum-noise computation in dual-pump fiber-optic phase-sensitive amplifiers
